name: National Infrastructure Failure
description: A coordinated cyber attack has crippled the eastern seaboard power grid, cascading into partial failures across water treatment networks and emergency communications. 2.5 million people are affected. Hospitals are on backup power. The attack vector is partially identified but not contained. Coordinate a multi-agency response under time pressure, incomplete information, and public scrutiny across six decision rounds.

actors.name: Emergency Management Director
actors.description: Top-level authority over cross-agency coordination. Can unlock federal resources with emergency declaration but creates immediate media attention.

actors.name: Regional Grid Operator (NERC)
actors.description: Controls physical restoration of the power grid. Restoration timeline depends on whether the cyber threat is isolated first.

actors.name: Metropolitan Water Authority
actors.description: Water treatment is 58% operational on auxiliary power. If power is not restored within 18 hours, chemical dosing systems fail.

actors.name: National Guard Commander
actors.description: Can deploy 4,000 personnel for logistics, security, and distribution. Requires emergency declaration to activate at full scale.

actors.name: Public Health Officer
actors.description: Monitors hospital capacity and population health. Triggers mass casualty protocols if medical_facility_status falls below 50.

actors.name: Communications Director
actors.description: Shapes public narrative. Full disclosure builds trust but risks panic. Managed messaging risks cover-up accusations.

actors.name: National Cyber Security Agency
actors.description: Currently at 35% confidence on attack attribution. Needs 2 rounds to reach 70% confidence. Recommends isolating affected systems before restoration.

actors.name: Regional Hospital Network Administrator
actors.description: Hospitals have 12–18 hours of backup generator fuel. Requesting priority power restoration and fuel resupply.

decision_points.title: Immediate Crisis Response Declaration
decision_points.description: The attack was confirmed 4 hours ago. Initial assessments are incomplete (35% confidence). You must decide the official response posture within the next 2 hours before public media cycles begin.

options.label: Declare national emergency — full federal resource activation
options.feedback: National emergency declared. Federal resources unlocked — FEMA, National Guard, and strategic reserves activated. Resource availability surges to 95%. However, media coverage has intensified and public unrest level has risen. Early panic buying reported at fuel stations.

options.label: Declare regional state of emergency — balanced response
options.feedback: Regional emergency declared. State-level resources activated including National Guard partial deployment. Balanced public messaging has maintained relative calm. Federal support available on request within 4–6 hours.

options.label: Handle internally — no formal emergency declaration yet
options.feedback: No formal declaration. Inter-agency coordination is slow and resources are limited. Public calm is maintained for now, but hospitals have flagged that generator fuel is running low. 3 hours have elapsed without formal coordination authority.

decision_points.title: Emergency Resource Prioritisation
decision_points.description: Resources are finite and infrastructure needs exceed capacity. You must decide which systems receive priority restoration support in the next operational cycle.

options.label: Prioritise hospitals and medical facilities
options.feedback: Hospital generator fuel resupply and dedicated circuit prioritisation has brought medical_facility_status to 98%. Power grid and water system continue degrading as other priorities take resources. Public health crisis averted for now.

options.label: Prioritise water treatment infrastructure
options.feedback: Water treatment restored to 78% — chemical dosing systems secured. A public health catastrophe from contamination is avoided. Hospitals have burned through additional generator reserves; medical_facility_status has dropped to 75%.

options.label: Prioritise communications restoration
options.feedback: Emergency communications restored to 88%. Agency coordination improves significantly to 55 — inter-agency information flow is now reliable. 911 services fully operational. Public trust increases as information becomes available.

options.label: Balanced allocation across all critical systems
options.feedback: Balanced allocation improves all systems incrementally but none reach critical recovery thresholds. Overall resilience is distributed but fragile. No single system is now at immediate risk of collapse.

decision_points.title: Public Communications Strategy
decision_points.description: Media is requesting a full briefing. The public is increasingly anxious. You have incomplete attack information (35% confidence). How do you communicate?

options.label: Full public disclosure — transparent briefing on all known facts
options.feedback: Transparency has built trust — public_trust rises to 78. However, disclosure of grid vulnerability details has caused hoarding and some localised unrest. Cyber security agency warns that disclosed technical details may assist the attacker.

options.label: Managed messaging — controlled narrative, withhold technical details
options.feedback: Controlled messaging maintains calm but media are questioning the withheld details. Public trust remains at 60. Two journalists have obtained partial information from agency leaks — cover-up risk is emerging.

options.label: Emergency broadcast only — minimal information, actionable instructions
options.feedback: Emergency broadcast provides instructions but no context. Public frustration is building — social media speculation is filling the information vacuum. Trust is declining. Unrest moderate.

decision_points.title: Inter-Agency Command Structure
decision_points.description: With multiple agencies responding, coordination is still fragmented. A command structure decision is needed to align resources.

options.label: Establish unified incident command (ICS/NIMS)
options.feedback: Unified incident command established under ICS framework. Agency coordination jumps to 80. Information flow is now structured and duplicated efforts eliminated. Takes 3 hours to stand up — time has advanced.

options.label: Lead agency model — Emergency Management Director takes command
options.feedback: Lead agency model established quickly. Director now has decision authority but three agencies have flagged jurisdictional concerns. Coordination is improved but not optimal — interoperability issues remain.

options.label: Federated coordination — agencies retain autonomy, share liaison officers
options.feedback: Federated model preserves agency autonomy and is implemented quickly. However, resource allocation conflicts continue and information remains siloed. Two agencies are executing conflicting recovery priorities.

decision_points.title: Cyber Threat Remediation Strategy
decision_points.description: The cyber security agency has reached 55–70% confidence on the attack vector. A remediation decision is now required before grid restoration can proceed safely.

options.label: Isolate all affected systems before restoration
options.feedback: Systems isolated. Threat contained. Grid restoration can now proceed without risk of re-infection. Isolation took 6 additional hours but the recovery path is now clean and secure.

options.label: Patch and restore concurrently — accept residual risk
options.feedback: Concurrent patching and restoration accelerates recovery — grid at 55% in 4 hours less than isolation approach. However, residual malware has been detected in 2 substations. Reinfection risk remains elevated.

options.label: Request federal cyber assistance before action
options.feedback: Federal cyber specialists arrived and fully characterised the attack within 6 hours. Threat attribution at 90% confidence. Clean remediation path identified but 8 additional hours elapsed. Grid restoration delayed.

decision_points.title: Public Recovery Timeline Commitment
decision_points.description: Media is demanding a restoration timeline. Your technical teams have given you a range of 48 hours to 8 days depending on risk posture. What do you communicate publicly?

options.label: Commit to aggressive 48-hour full restoration timeline
options.feedback: Public confidence boosted by decisive commitment. Teams are under pressure to deliver. If the 48-hour target is missed, the credibility impact will be severe. Current trajectory suggests 60–70% grid restoration within the window.

options.label: Moderate 5-day estimate with daily public updates
options.feedback: Moderate timeline is credible and allows operational flexibility. Daily briefings maintain public confidence. Some impatience but no significant unrest. Trust holding steady at 72.

options.label: Conservative estimate with full uncertainty disclosure
options.feedback: Full uncertainty disclosure maintains honesty but increases public anxiety. Unrest level has risen to 28. The media has characterised the response as 'confused'. Opposition parties are calling for an independent inquiry.

event.title: Public Health Emergency — Water Contamination Risk
event.description: Water treatment has fallen below safe operational threshold. Chemical dosing failure detected. Boil-water advisory issued across 3 municipalities.

event.title: Civil Unrest Incidents Reported
event.description: Police report civil disturbances at 4 distribution points. National Guard deployment requested to maintain order. Operational resources diverted.

event.title: Hospital Network Critical Alert
event.description: Three hospitals have declared internal emergencies. Elective procedures suspended. Emergency department diversions in effect. Two ICU patients at risk.

event.title: Inter-Agency Coordination Breakdown
event.description: Emergency Management Director reports that two agencies have begun independent operations conflicting with the unified response plan. Resource duplication detected.

event.title: Grid Recovery Momentum Achieved
event.description: Power restoration above 65% creates cascading improvements — water treatment pumps restart, emergency communications improve, and hospitals reduce generator dependency.

event.title: Cyber Reinfection Detected
event.description: Malware re-propagation detected in grid control systems during restoration. Emergency cyber isolation protocols activated, setting back recovery by several hours.

outcome_conditions.description: Hospital network has collapsed below safe operating threshold. Mass casualty protocols declared. Federal disaster declaration with full liability implications.
Water treatment failure is complete. Public health emergency affecting 2.5M people. Multi-agency investigation and congressional hearings initiated.
Public trust has collapsed. Government credibility crisis. Political leadership facing calls for resignation. Independent inquiry commissioned.
Critical infrastructure has been restored to safe operational levels. Recovery operations transitioning to normalisation phase. Public confidence stabilising.
Full infrastructure restoration with maintained public trust. Crisis response widely viewed as effective. Post-incident review and lessons-learned process initiated.
